name: Striped hyena
description:
3D scan of the skull of a striped hyena (*Hyaena hyaena*). 

The striped hyena is a species of hyena native to North and East Africa, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia and Indian subcontinent. It is the smallest of the bone-cracking hyenas, having a smaller and less specialised skull. The Body length can range from 85 to 130 cm and the tail measures 25-40 cm. It is primarily a scavenger which feeds mainly on ungulate carcasses in different stages of decomposition, fresh bones, cartilages, ligaments, and bone marrow.


Specimen: Striped hyena, *Hyaena hyaena* (Linnaeus, 1758)

Inventory number: C 1391

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Simone Farina

name: 3D Fox Head
description:
I’ve wanted to make something like this for a long time because I love foxes, and I’m so happy with how it turned out! I started by sculpting the model in ZBrush, beginning with a rough shape and slowly refining the details. Once I was happy with the sculpt, I retopologized it to make the model cleaner and easier to work with. Then, I created the UVs so I could paint the textures properly without any stretching or distortion. For the texturing, I hand-painted everything using my own 2D art style. I wanted it to have a unique, hand drawn look. At the end I set up a simple rig to give it an Idle animation. It was a fun challenge to bring my painting style into 3D, and I learned a lot in the process. Seeing it all come together was really exciting, and I’m so proud of the final result!

Edit! I returned to this project a few months later to update the textures, re render and I'm very happy with how it turn out!

name: IGC0209_Hoploscaphites_nodosus_[high]
description:
Este fóssil é um exemplo de um amonoide do gênero *Hoploscaphites*, característico do Cretáceo Superior. *Hoploscaphites* é conhecido por sua concha espiralada com ornamentações bem definidas, como as ranhuras radiais visíveis no modelo 3D. Essas costelas pronunciadas são uma característica distintiva deste gênero. *Hoploscaphites* é um importante fóssil-guia para o Cretáceo Superior.

**Classificação**: Metazoa, Mollusca, Cephalopoda, Ammonoidea, Ancyloceratina, Scaphitidae

**Localidade**: EUA, South Dakota, Wasta

**Contexto geológico**: Folhelho Pierre

**Idade**: Fanerozoico, Mesozoico, Cretáceo, Cretáceo Superior

**Tamanho**: 3 cm (maior comprimento)

**Designação original**: Acanthoscaphites nodosus

**Material de apoio**: LANDMAN, Neil H. et al. Scaphites of the “nodosus group” from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) of the Western Interior of North America. Bull. Am. Mus. Nat. Hist., v. 2010, n. 342, p. 1-242, 2010.

**Digitalização**: Shining 3D EinScan SE V2

**Escala**: 1:1

name: Model 111A - Imperial Woodpecker on Tree
description:
This is a 3D animation of an Imperial Woodpecker (Campephilus imperialis) climbing and pecking at a pine tree.  The Imperial Woodpecker was a very large (up to 60 cm wing length), and now extinct woodpecker previously found in Pine woodlands of Northern Mexico.  Deforestation and habitat change likely sped its decline.  The 3D model was reconstructed by CG artist Johnson Martin and UMASS Amherst PhD student Josh Medina using Blender and other software.

John McCormick from Occidential College provided funding and guidance.  The specimen was reconstructed from a 3D photogrammetry scan of a preserved Imperial Woodpecker from the Moore Lab of Ornithology, as well as from a single video of an Imperial Woodpecker flying from the Cornell Lab of Ornithology.

Downloads are freely available for creative and non-profit use. To inquire about licensing, please visit www.digitallife3d.org.

name: Boi Caprichoso Festival Folclórico de Parintins
description: O Boi Caprichoso é uma agremiação folclórica que participa do Festival Folclórico de Parintins, um evento cultural de grande importância na Amazônia. Com suas cores azul e branco, Caprichoso encanta o público com apresentações que misturam dança, música, e encenações teatrais, sempre focando na rica herança cultural e nas lendas da região amazônica. Fundado em 1913, o Boi Caprichoso tem uma longa história de celebração da cultura local, e seus membros, conhecidos como "brincantes", se dedicam a criar espetáculos deslumbrantes que honram e preservam as tradições da Amazônia. A cada ano, Caprichoso compete com seu rival, Boi Garantido, em uma exibição de criatividade, paixão e habilidade artística, tornando o festival uma experiência única e vibrante.

description:

I couldn't decide between a cat or a bear, so we combined them to make this little guy. Potato has the ears of both a bear and a cat, little stumpy kitty paws, and a small, fluffy bear tail. The patches and fluffy collar were added for fun, but the bandages were added as a result of a vicious puppy attack! His belly was weighted with tiny polypropylene beads, so being the kid I was a couple bandages seemed like the best solution :P
I made this model to express a precious and valuable memory of mine<3

name: American Cockroach - insect
description: The American cockroach (Periplaneta americana) is among the largest and most resilient cockroach species. Despite its name, it originated in Africa and spread globally. It thrives in warm, humid environments and is commonly found in basements, sewers, and kitchens. Growing up to 53mm, it has a reddish-brown exoskeleton, long antennae, and fully developed wings, though it rarely flies. It is an omnivorous scavenger, feeding on decaying organic matter, starches, and even non-food items like paper. Highly adaptable, it can survive weeks without food and endure harsh conditions. Cockroaches play a role in decomposition but are also vectors for bacteria like Salmonella and allergens that can trigger asthma. Their rapid reproduction and resilience make them difficult pests to control. Despite their reputation, cockroaches are evolutionary marvels, existing for over 300 million years. Studying them has led to insights in robotics and medicine, proving their importance beyond their pest status.

name: Cnidaire - Siderastraea sp.
description:
**Nom**  : *Siderastraea sp.*

**Classe** : Anthozoa.

**Ordre**: Scleractinia.

**Famille**: Siderastreidae.

**Description**:  Accumulation de thalles sans géométrie particulière, bien conservés, pris dans une matrice calcaire. Chaque corallite est composé de plusieurs septas (cloisons internes) reliés par un columella au centre.  Les squelettes sont constitués d’aragonite. *Siderestraea* est souvent trouvé en association avec d’autres coraux, éponges, mollusques, et invertébrés marins  des environnements récifaux.

**Localité**: Non renseignée.

**Dimensions** :  12 cm de longueur.

**Âge**: Campanien (Crétacé supérieur) au Pléistocène.

**Méthode** : Photogrammétrie avec Agisoft metashape.

**Réalisation**: APEX UniLaSalle / Collection du Musée Albert de Lapparent : https://www.musee-delapparent.com/fr/echantillons/fossiles

name: Cozy Garden Fountain
description:
I made this little diorama as part of a 3-week sprint course I did from Into Games; Creating A 3D Garden Feature with Anya Elvidge. I wanted to improve my sculpting and handpainted texturing skills so I designed my scene to have lots of different materials on which I could practice. name: Eurasian blue tit
description:
Барвисте оперення 🎨
Блакитна синиця має яскраво-жовтий живіт, синю спину та білу голову з синьою "шапочкою". Її забарвлення допомагає маскуватися серед листя, особливо навесні та влітку.
Гнучкість і спритність 🤸‍♂️
Вона вміє висіти догори лапами, шукаючи їжу під листям або на гілках. Завдяки своїй спритності блакитні синиці можуть дістатися до їжі в місцях, недоступних для більших птахів.
Розумні та кмітливі 🧠
У 20 столітті в Англії блакитні синиці навчилися відкривати кришки пляшок з молоком, щоб дістатися до вершків. Це приклад соціального навчання серед птахів.
Висока плодовитість 🐣
У кладці блакитної синиці може бути до 12 яєць, а іноді навіть більше. Це допомагає компенсувати високий рівень смертності серед молодих птахів.
Віддані батьки 👨‍👩‍👦
Самка висиджує яйця, а самець у цей час годує її. Після вилуплення обидва батьки активно приносять корм пташенятам, роблячи це до 900 разів на день!

name: Toque macaque
description:
3D scan of a skull of toque macaque (*Macaca sinica*). 

The toque macaque is an Old World monkey endemic to Sri Lanka. The head and body length ranges from 40 to 47,5 cm with male larger than female. It feeds mainly on fruits, but also flowers, mushrooms, and prey items.


Specimen: toque macaque, *Macaca sinica* (Linneaus, 1771)

Inventory number: 1787

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Marco Merella

name: Pygmy sperm whale skull
description:
This is the skull from a pygmy sperm whale (*Kogia breviceps*) that was collected from a stranded animal at Dolphin Sands on the Freycinet Peninsula in 2019. 

Pygmy sperm whales are rarely sighted at sea and little is known of their ecology or behaviour. Examination of stranded animals indicates that their diet is mainly composed of deep-water squid, small fish and crustaceans. Examination of feeding in captive animals indicates that these small whales primarily capture small prey using suction, similar to their gigantic relative - the sperm whales (*Physeter macrocephalus*). 

**Museum Collection:** [Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery](https://www.tmag.tas.gov.au/)

**Registration number:**  TMAG A8362

Scan created in the app PolyCam on an iPhone 15 Pro by Dr David Hocking (Senior Curator of Vertebrate Zoology and Palaeontology, TMAG).

name: lymphadenopathy in a dog
description:
Historical wax model showing generalized lymphadenopathy in a dog

size of specimen: 409.1 x 247.8 x 57 mm

3D scanning performed with the structured light scanner Artec Space Spider

Pathogenesis: Infectious agents (e.g. Mycobacterium spp., Leishmania, Ehrlichia, Bartonella) spread hematogenously or via lymphatics, causing reactive or granulomatous lymph node hyperplasia. Nodes may be enlarged, necrotic, abscessed, or fibrotic depending on the cause.

Etiology: Usually bacterial, protozoal, or fungal infections; may also be immune-mediated or paraneoplastic.

Epidemiology: Occasional, depending on region and exposure (e.g. travel-associated diseases).

Clinical Features: Fever, lethargy, localized or generalized lymphadenopathy; possible dysphagia, dyspnea, or skin changes.

Diagnostics: Fine-needle aspirate, cytology, biopsy, PCR, culture; supported by serology and imaging.

name: Obedience… or Oddity?
description:
Unearthed at a flea market in Southern France, this mysterious vintage action figure set—featuring an anthropomorphic dog and a kneeling human with a treat on his nose—has collectors and artists equally baffled.

No brand. No markings. No packaging.
Just two worn-out plastic figures, a dog in a red tank top, and a man kneeling with a magnetic, removable dog treat perfectly balanced on his face.

Was this a forgotten toy line from the late '70s or early '80s? A one-off satirical art piece? Or maybe something that was never meant to be sold at all?

All we know is:
It exists. It’s strange. And we kind of love it.

Would you display this in your home—or hide it in the attic forever?

name: Megaraptor namunhuaiquii
description:
*Megaraptor namunhuaiquii* was a large theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Patagonia, Argentina, during the Late Cretaceous period, roughly 90 million years ago. It's best known for its enormous hand claws, some over 35 centimeters long, originally mistaken for foot claws similar to those of dromaeosaurs when the species was first described in 1998.

Estimated at around 8 meters long, *Megaraptor* belonged to a group called Megaraptora, whose exact placement among theropods is still debated. Some studies link them to tyrannosauroids, while others place them closer to allosauroids or as an early-diverging branch of their own.

Unlike the short arms of other large theropods, *Megaraptor* had long, powerful forelimbs built for grasping, suggesting it relied on those massive hooked claws to snag prey. Fossils come mainly from the Portezuelo Formation, offering a glimpse into the diverse predator community of Cretaceous South America.

name: Cyclophorus crosseanus - MNCN-15.05/3217
description:
**Description**: *Cyclophorus crosseanus* (Hidalgo, 1866) (Syntype). Collected in Ecuador by the Scientific Commission of the Pacific (1862–1866): a major 19th-century Spanish expedition. Aided by a naval squadron, naturalists traveled across South America and California, collecting over 80,000 natural specimens. The mission culminated in an overland trek across the Andes and Amazon. Notably, they collected 40,000 mollusks, yielding 35 newly described species now preserved at the MNCN.

**Specimen**: *Cyclophorus crosseanus* (Hidalgo, 1866)

**Inventory number**: MNCN-15.05/3217

**Collection**: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, Malacología. Curators: Lola Bragado (lolab@mncn.csic.es) and Javier de Andrés Cobeta (javiermol@mncn.csic.es)

**More about**:

Find more about the MNCN [here](http:mncn.csic.es/en).

Scanned with an Artec Spider in 20246 by Leticia Herrera and Carlos A. Palancar.

name: Giant Ground Sloth  ( eremotherium aurillardi )
description:
Eremotherium laurillardi was one of the largest giant ground sloths to ever live, reaching lengths of up to 6 m and weights of several tonnes during the Pleistocene. A member of the family Megatheriidae, it inhabited much of North and South America and fed on leaves, branches, and other vegetation. This specimen (USNM V20867) was collected in Herrera Province, Panama, in 1951 and is housed in the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. Giant ground sloths became extinct near the end of the Ice Age, around 11,700 years ago.

Source model: Smithsonian Institution, National Museum of Natural History (USNM V20867).
Original scan released under CC0 Public Domain. Smithsonian source data available through the Smithsonian Open Access program.

name: Vince - Deep Sea Inspired Character
description:
Vince is a character design influenced by deep-sea ecosystems, taking inspiration from creatures such as sea slugs, shrimp, yeti crabs, and thermal vent tube worms. His design also incorporates rocky textures and marine-inspired forms to create a character that reflects the strange beauty of the deep ocean.

This model was developed as part of a series of school projects and highlights my skills in character design, modeling, texturing, UV unwrapping, lighting, and rendering. While the piece is ready for presentation, it remains a work in progress—I plan to revisit this character in the future to explore adding features like hair simulation to expand its design possibilities further.

This project was created using Maya, ZBrush, Substance Painter, Photoshop, and Procreate.

name: Frog brooch
description:
**Collection:** Roman Archeology Dept.
 
**Inv.-No.:** [CAR-M-7391](https://www.online.landessammlungen-noe.at/objects/1485256)

**Material:** Bronze, enamel 

**Dimensions:** 3,8 cm

**Dating:** 2nd quarter of the 1st - end of the 3rd century AD 

The image depicts a frog with bent legs, in a seemingly resting position. The toes are indicated by notches, with three of them only partially preserved. The frog’s body, typically bent (possibly suggesting the sacral joint), has a light green, enamel-coated underside, with six small turquoise depressions filled with enamel. The lateral eyes are sculpturally represented. The hinge construction is partially preserved, but the pin is missing. The laterally positioned eyes, the central decorated band, and the lateral wart ridges on the back could suggest that it is a brown frog, possibly a moor frog.

This object was digitized through the 'Kulturerbe digital' program of the Federal Ministry for Arts, Culture, Public Service and Sport.

name: Acorn weevil (Curculio)
description:
3D scan of a *Curculio* L. 1758 acorn weevil or nut weevil (Coleoptera: Curculionidae) from Cologne, Germany. 

I used a PiScAnt - a Raspberry Pi-powered version of the original [ScAnt](https://doi.org/10.7717%2Fpeerj.11155). A Nikon EL-Nikkor 50mm 1:2.8 lens was used in reverse on the Rapsberry Pi HQ Cam.

3600 images were taken and stacked to 300 views with [Zerene Stacker](https://www.zerenesystems.com/) (DMap). 3D spatial data was photogrammetrically created in [Agisoft Metashape](https://www.agisoft.com/).

name: Esqueleto ballena jorobada joven 🐋
description:
La ballena jorobada (megaptera novaeangliae) es un cetáceo migratorio conocido por sus largas aletas pectorales y espectaculares saltos. Los adultos miden 12-16 m y pesan 25-40 toneladas. Esta especie se alimenta de krill y peces usando técnicas como redes de burbujas. Cada año migra desde aguas polares a zonas tropicales como el Pacífico colombiano (julio-noviembre), donde los juveniles suelen acercarse a la costa. En la exhibición permanente de biología  se conserva el esqueleto de un ejemplar juvenil de aproximadamente 18 metros, casi completo; aunque carece del coxis una pequeña estructura vestigial que recuerda su ascendencia mamífera y terrestre, permite admirar su colosal anatomía y comprender mejor su adaptación a la vida marina.

This is a digital replica of the 3D printed parts in our [Dogfish Shark Skull Active Learning Kit](https://3das.us/shop/dogfish-skull-kit/), a resource that helps students learn shark skull form and function with [hands-on activities](https://3das.us/category/guides/dogfish-guides/dogfish-skull-guides/). The color coding in this model matches the kit. Labial cartilages (orange) have been added to the digital model but are not included in the kit. Hooks and pegs on the 3D printed parts for attachments of muscles and ligaments have been removed in this digital model.

For commercial use of this model, please contact us at contact@3danatomystudios.com.

name: Murray Cod
description: The Murray cod (Maccullochella peelii) is a large Australian predatory freshwater fish of the genus Maccullochella in the family Percichthyidae. Although the species is called a cod in the vernacular, it is not related to the Northern Hemisphere marine cod (Gadus) species. The Murray cod is an important part of Australia's vertebrate wildlife—as an apex predator in the Murray-Darling River system—and also significant in Australia's human culture. The Murray cod is the largest exclusively freshwater fish in Australia, and one of the largest in the world. Other common names for Murray cod include cod, greenfish, goodoo, Mary River cod, Murray perch, ponde, pondi and Queensland freshwater cod.

name: Brown dorcopsis
description:
3D scan of the skull of a brown dorcopsis (*Dorcopsis muelleri*).

The brown dorcopsis is a marsupial that lives in West New Guinea and the nearby Indonesian islands in West Papua in swampy tropical lowland forest including areas that flood in the rainy season, and it is believed to be tolerant of secondary forest. Males are larger than females: : the head and body length is 70-78 cm in males and 54-65 cm in females. The dorsal colour is dull brown, chocolate brown, reddish brown or fawn and the underparts are whitish, creamy-yellow or greyish. The arms are sometimes paler than the dorsal surface and the tip of the tail is devoid of hair. 

Specimen Brown dorcopsis, *Dorcopsis muelleri* (Lesson, 1827)

Inventory number: C 992

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

name: BIOARQUITECTURA 2 CORTE
description:
Modelos elaborados en el marco del trabajo de grado ***“Mundos plausibles y bioarquitecturas: Modelos de simulación para la coevolución entre sistemas ecológicos habitables”***, desarrollado como requisito para optar al título de Arquitecta en la Pontificia Universidad Javeriana, Facultad de Arquitectura y Diseño.

Estas bioarquitecturas fueron construidas en el entorno del *videojuego Minecraft y exportadas mediante la herramienta Mineways*, como parte de una metodología de simulación computacional orientada a explorar configuraciones espaciales adaptativas, ecosistémicamente sensibles y plausibles desde una perspectiva biocéntrica. Los modelos se utilizaron en procesos de simulación bioarquitectónica aplicados a mundos posibles, y forman parte del componente experimental de la investigación. Para conocer en profundidad la propuesta y su desarrollo, la tesis completa se encuentra disponible en el repositorio de la universidad.

name: Seath the Scaleless
description:
Seath the Scaleless is a visually striking and grotesque dragon from Dark Souls, known for his eerie, otherworldly appearance. This 3D model captures his distinctive features in stunning detail, staying true to his in-game depiction while enhancing his intricate design for a more immersive experience.
The model showcases Seath's pale, translucent flesh, which replaces traditional dragon scales, giving him an almost spectral, albino appearance. His massive, deformed wings are tattered and warped, resembling crystalline appendages rather than functional wings. Jagged, glowing crystals protrude from his body, particularly along his spine and lower torso, symbolizing his deep connection to sorcery and the Primordial Crystal that grants him immortality.
Sorry for another long break, life happens i guess. Anyway he is one my favorite bosses from DS1 so i decided to make him.

name: Hippopotamus
description:
3D scan of the mandible of an adult Hippopotamus (*Hippopotamus amphibius*). 

The hippopotamus is a large semiaquatic mammal native to sub-Saharan Africa. Adults average weight is 1,500 kg and are 2.90 to 5.05 m long. Despite its stocky shape and short legs, it is capable of running 30 km/h over short distances.  It inhabits rivers, lakes, and mangrove swamps where spends most the day in water to stay cool and hydrated. Just before night begins, they leave the water to forage on land. Its diet consists almost entirely of grass, with only minimal consumption of aquatic plants.




Specimen: Hippopotamus, *Hippopotamus amphibius* Linnaeus, 1758

The African penguin is a species of penguin confined to southern African waters. Like all penguins, it is flightless, with a streamlined body and wings stiffened and flattened into flippers for a marine habitat. Adults weigh an average of 2.2–3.5 kg and are 60–70 cm (24–28 in) tall. It is a pursuit diver and feeds primarily on fish and squid. The average lifespan of an African penguin is 10 to around 25 years in the wild and the primary predators of African penguins at sea include sharks and fur seals.

The name comes from its resemblance to the decorative “keman” used in Buddhist temples, and its ribs are stronger than those of the kemangai. It lives in sandy bottoms in the middle of the intertidal zone to a depth of 20 meters. In Okinawa, it is targeted for shellfish gathering.
